Since it is wall-mounted and flat, the lack of a top surface is expected, so it reads as front_elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of hanging stalactites under a rocky band. It shows about 4-5 lightness steps (pale highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) with speckled grain on the rock and per-spike shading, so it is not a flat body with one shade. Measured facts: 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which sits between the hedge (9) and the stall (17) and well (20); 0% near-flat coverage, so there are no flat fills. The 37% near-neutral dark edge share is close to the bench (44%) and well (33%), so the edges lean tinted and are not a uniform black sticker outline. Density is a little below the richest references (well, stall), but a thin, sparse hanging prop should not fail for that alone. A careful artist would accept it next to the references, though it is not quite as rich as the well or stall.
